_about: What gear-outfit recommends for each answer. Forks replace this file. Each entry is a plan line without accepted, and means says what changes in practice.

autonomy.ask: How much should Claude do before checking with you?

check-in.why: You want to see each risky action

lines.means: Sessions ask before each risky action, in place of the classifier

auto.why: A classifier decides what needs you, so routine work doesn't stop

lines.means: Sessions start in auto mode, where a classifier blocks risky actions and the rest run without a prompt. It's already the default on recent versions, so this pins it

git-and-prs.ask: May Claude push branches and open PRs without asking?

own-repos.why: Work in repos you own shouldn't stop for a prompt

lines.means: The classifier treats these organizations as yours, so writing to their issues and PRs stops counting as an external write

cost-versus-quality.ask: Which matters more, cost or the best answer?

cost.why: A lower effort level spends less on routine work

lines.means: Sessions on this model think less by default, and you can raise it per session

quality.why: A higher effort level suits hard work

lines.means: Sessions on this model think harder by default, and cost more

stack.ask: Which languages do you work in? Check what's on the machine first.

typescript.why: A language server gives Claude symbols and diagnostics, at almost no startup cost
typescript.note: Needs typescript-language-server, and a project-level typescript that ships tsserver. TypeScript 7 doesn't.

lines.means: Claude can ask the TypeScript server about code

python.why: A language server gives Claude symbols and diagnostics, at almost no startup cost

lines.means: Claude can ask the Python server about code

rust.why: A language server gives Claude symbols and diagnostics, at almost no startup cost

lines.means: Claude can ask the Rust server about code

go.why: A language server gives Claude symbols and diagnostics, at almost no startup cost

lines.means: Claude can ask the Go server about code

solo-or-team.ask: Is this repo yours alone, or shared with a team?

team.why: Shared rules belong in the repo's .claude/settings.json, which this skill doesn't write

public-or-private.ask: Is your work public, private, or a mix?

public.why: State which repos are public, so the classifier judges what's safe to push

lines.means: The classifier knows which pushes publish, without having to guess
